issues.summary: One-page checkout
description: ## Why
Our checkout takes three steps and loses a third of the people who start it. Most of them leave on the delivery step, where we ask for the address a second time.
## What
One page with address, delivery and payment, and the order summary beside it. Vouchers apply without a reload. The old checkout stays behind a flag until the new one wins.
## How we know it worked
- Checkout conversion above 3.3 % for two weeks at 50 % of sessions
- No rise in payment errors
- Support tickets about vouchers go down, not up
Requirements: [[page:PROD/One-page checkout]]

comments.body: Fine by me. The flag lives in summit, not in the template, so we can turn it off without a deploy.
First layouts are in the design file. The summary sits on the right on desktop and folds into a bar at the bottom on phones. Feedback very welcome before Friday.
Week 3 at 50 %: conversion 3.6 % against 2.8 % on the old flow. @s-lena, how do the voucher tickets look?
Two voucher tickets this week, both about [[WEB-44]]. Last month we had eleven. I would call that a win.

issues.summary: Collect address, delivery and payment on one page
description: As a customer I want to enter everything on one page, so that I see what is left and do not lose my input when I go back.
## Acceptance
- [x] Address, delivery and payment are sections of one form
- [x] A section that is complete folds into one line with an Edit link
- [x] Going back in the browser keeps what was typed
- [ ] The page works without JavaScript, with a full reload per section
The layout:
![The one-page checkout](lib:checkout-one-page)

comments.body: The form is server-rendered now and each section posts on its own. Without JavaScript it reloads, with it the section swaps in place. Tested on the small phone and the big tablet.
Looks great. Tiny nudge: the folded sections need a bit more space above them, 16 px instead of 8, or they read as one block.
Done, and the Edit links are real links now, so the keyboard reaches them.
Tested on staging with 14 test orders. One problem: the delivery section forgets the pick-up shop after a failed payment. Filed as part of [[WEB-13]].
Reviewing. The handler is long but readable. Two comments in the merge request, nothing blocking.

issues.summary: Feature flag for the one-page checkout, at 50 % of sessions
description: The flag is stored per session, so a customer does not switch checkouts halfway. Sessions are split by a hash of the session id.
```go
func OnePageCheckout(sessionID string, percent int) bool {
h := fnv.New32a()
h.Write([]byte(sessionID))
return int(h.Sum32()%100) < percent

issues.summary: Remember the address of a returning customer
A voucher code applied twice doubles the discount
description: Steps on staging:
1. Add the Firn 30 backpack to the cart
2. Enter `FIRSTSNOW` and press Apply
3. Press Apply again before the first answer arrives
Expected: one discount of 20 %. Actual: two discounts, the total drops from CHF 149.00 to CHF 95.36.

comments.body: Found it! Two requests race, and both read the cart before either writes. The fix is a unique index on `(cart_id, voucher_code)` and an upsert. No more double helpings.
Tested with five quick clicks and two tabs. One discount every time. Merci, closing.
